task.title: Single-flight stale refresh
task.specification: Config ttl>=1,stale>=0. Start now=0, empty cache/pending and next token=1. Events get{key},resolve{key,token,value},reject{key,token},invalidate{key},advance{dt>=0}. On get return cached value only if age<ttl+stale, else null. If no cache or age>=ttl and no pending for key, emit {key,token:next} and increment next. Cached data remains stored even after stale window. Matching resolve stores value at now and clears pending; matching reject only clears pending; unmatched response ignored. Invalidate clears cache and pending but never rewinds next token. Advance only changes now. Only get returns nonnull value; others return null. Output {value,fetch:[{key,token}],pending:[sorted pending keys],now}. Equality at ttl triggers refresh, equality at ttl+stale cannot return stale data. Implement pure solve({config,state,event})->{state,output}, initially state=null. Only the current event is supplied; every named event uses a type field, e.g. {type:"restore"}. Return exactly the stated output fields each step; opaque JSON state is not graded. All numeric inputs and intermediate arithmetic are safe integers; time deltas are nonnegative. Unless a task explicitly overrides this, keys, snapshot IDs, readers and graph nodes are single lowercase ASCII letters. Integral JSON number spellings such as 1 and 1.0 are equivalent; booleans remain distinct from numbers. At most eight identities and 48 events occur. Configurations and event fields shown below are present. Ordinary regimes use moderate storage and timing; boundary uses equality/empty states; adversarial repeats stale/conflicting events; shift uses smaller capacity, longer timing gaps or deeper dependency shapes, without changing these rules. Generator regimes: Boundary ttl=2,stale=0; shift ttl=4,stale=2 versus ordinary ttl=2,stale=3, with clock gaps 0..7 instead of 0..5, retaining both fresh and stale behavior. Adversarial traces add adjacent repeated events, capped at 48; those events obey the same contract.

matchedCard.label: Lighthouse sector signals
matchedCard.relation: A navigational source can provide a general identifying signal and a separate directional indication for a particular hazard. What a sector indication signifies depends on the observer's position and its relationship to the marked region.
assumptions: The source and the meaning of its sector can be identified.
The observer has sufficient visibility and positional context to interpret the indication.
matchedCard.boundary: A sector signal describes only its designated region. An ordinary indication does not certify that every nearby route is hazard-free, and poor visibility can limit interpretation.
matchedCard.source_fact: Trinity House describes Start Point's white navigational flashes and a separate red sector marking the shallow Skerries Bank, alongside a low-visibility hazard warning signal.

sources.title: Trinity House completes re-engineering of Start Point Lighthouse

shuffledCard.label: Cartographic generalization
shuffledCard.relation: At a smaller representation scale, selection, simplification, and combination can preserve legibility while omitting detail. The resulting representation depends on scale and purpose; omission from that representation does not establish absence from the represented world.
assumptions: The representation has a specified scale and communicative purpose.
A more detailed source contains distinctions from which the representation is derived.
shuffledCard.boundary: Simplification can remove a distinction important for another purpose. A reduced representation cannot recover information that it does not encode.
shuffledCard.source_fact: USGS describes cartographic generalization as selecting and reducing detail to produce representations appropriate to scale.

initial.explanation: The rule is single-flight caching: freshness is age < ttl; stale data remains visible while age < ttl+stale, and at most one refresh may be pending per key. A response affects state only when its key and token match. For example, after ttl=2 and a resolve at time 0, time 2 must trigger a refresh rather than return the value.
initial.mapping: now is current time; c[key]=[value,storedTime]; p[key]=pending token; n is the next token. A get reads c when age < ttl+stale and starts a fetch exactly when age >= ttl and no matching pending request exists.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the stated schema, safe-integer bounds, and JSON-value restrictions. Keys are lowercase ASCII as specified. The implementation treats cached null as a stored value.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;var q={now:0,c:{},p:{},n:1},T=input.config.ttl,S=input.config.stale;for(var i=0;i<input.events.length;i++){var e=input.events[i],o=output[i],f=[],v=null,k=e.key;if(e.type==='get'){var x=q.c[k],a=x?q.now-x[1]:0;if(x&&a<T+S)v=x[0];if((!x||a>=T)&&q.p[k]===undefined){q.p[k]=q.n;f=[{key:k,token:q.n++}]}}else if(e.type==='resolve'&&q.p[k]===e.token){q.c[k]=[e.value,q.now];delete q.p[k]}else if(e.type==='reject'&&q.p[k]===e.token)delete q.p[k];else if(e.type==='invalidate'){delete q.c[k];delete q.p[k]}else if(e.type==='advance')q.now+=e.dt;var p=Object.keys(q.p).sort();if(!o||o.now!==q.now||o.value!==v||JSON.stringify(o.fetch)!==JSON.stringify(f)||JSON.stringify(o.pending)!==JSON.stringify(p))return false}return true}
initial.program: function solve(x){var C=x.config,e=x.event,s=x.state;if(s===null)s={now:0,c:{},p:{},n:1};var f=[],v=null,k=e.key,t=e.type;if(t==='get'){var z=s.c[k],a=z?s.now-z[1]:0;if(z&&a<C.ttl+C.stale)v=z[0];if((!z||a>=C.ttl)&&s.p[k]===undefined){s.p[k]=s.n;f.push({key:k,token:s.n++})}}else if(t==='resolve'&&s.p[k]===e.token){s.c[k]=[e.value,s.now];delete s.p[k]}else if(t==='reject'&&s.p[k]===e.token)delete s.p[k];else if(t==='invalidate'){delete s.c[k];delete s.p[k]}else if(t==='advance')s.now+=e.dt;return{state:s,output:{value:v,fetch:f,pending:Object.keys(s.p).sort(),now:s.now}}}

final.explanation: Implements single-flight stale caching. Cached entries remain stored after expiry, stale values are visible only before ttl+stale, and refresh begins at age >= ttl when no request is pending. Responses affect state only when their key and token match; invalidation clears both cache and pending state without rewinding tokens.
final.program: function solve(x){var c=x.config,e=x.event,s=x.state;if(s===null)s={now:0,c:{},p:{},n:1};var f=[],v=null,k=e.key,t=e.type;if(t==='get'){var z=s.c[k],a=z?s.now-z[1]:0;if(z&&a<c.ttl+c.stale)v=z[0];if((!z||a>=c.ttl)&&s.p[k]===undefined){s.p[k]=s.n;f.push({key:k,token:s.n});s.n++}}else if(t==='resolve'&&s.p[k]===e.token){s.c[k]=[e.value,s.now];delete s.p[k]}else if(t==='reject'&&s.p[k]===e.token)delete s.p[k];else if(t==='invalidate'){delete s.c[k];delete s.p[k]}else if(t==='advance')s.now+=e.dt;return{state:s,output:{value:v,fetch:f,pending:Object.keys(s.p).sort(),now:s.now}}}

initial.explanation: Implement a single-flight cache with fresh and stale visibility windows. Cached entries remain stored after expiry; refreshes are deduplicated by pending key, and only matching responses affect state.
initial.mapping: The cache maps keys to {value,time}; pending maps keys to tokens; now is logical time and next is the monotonic token counter. Get computes age against ttl and ttl+stale.
initial.assumptions: Inputs obey the stated event, numeric, and JSON constraints. Values are preserved exactly, including false, zero, empty strings, objects, arrays, and null.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;var keys={};for(var i=0;i<input.events.length;i++){var e=input.events[i];if(e.type==='get')keys[e.key]=1;var o=output[i];if(!o||!Array.isArray(o.fetch)||!Array.isArray(o.pending)||typeof o.now!=='number'||!('value'in o))return false;for(var j=0;j<o.fetch.length;j++){var f=o.fetch[j];if(!f||!keys[f.key]||typeof f.token!=='number')return false}for(var k=1;k<o.pending.length;k++)if(o.pending[k-1]>o.pending[k])return false}return true}
initial.program: function solve(x){var c=x.config,e=x.event,s=x.state;if(s===null)s={now:0,next:1,cache:{},pending:{}};var out={value:null,fetch:[],pending:[],now:s.now};if(e.type==='advance')s.now+=e.dt;else if(e.type==='get'){var z=s.cache[e.key],age=z===undefined?Infinity:s.now-z.t;if(z!==undefined&&age<c.ttl+c.stale)out.value=z.v;if((z===undefined||age>=c.ttl)&&s.pending[e.key]===undefined){var tok=s.next++;s.pending[e.key]=tok;out.fetch.push({key:e.key,token:tok})}}else if(e.type==='resolve'){if(s.pending[e.key]===e.token){s.cache[e.key]={v:e.value,t:s.now};delete s.pending[e.key]}}else if(e.type==='reject'){if(s.pending[e.key]===e.token)delete s.pending[e.key];}else if(e.type==='invalidate'){delete s.cache[e.key];delete s.pending[e.key]}out.now=s.now;var p=Object.keys(s.pending);p.sort();out.pending=p;return{state:s,output:out}}

final.explanation: Implements logical time, cached values with fresh/stale visibility, single-flight refreshes, monotonic fetch tokens, matching response handling, invalidation, and sorted pending keys. State is initialized only when the host supplies null; all event outputs contain exactly value, fetch, pending, and now.
final.program: function solve(x){var c=x.config,e=x.event,s=x.state;if(s===null)s={now:0,next:1,cache:{},pending:{}};var out={value:null,fetch:[],pending:[],now:s.now};if(e.type==='advance'){s.now+=e.dt}else if(e.type==='get'){var z=s.cache[e.key],has=z!==undefined,age=has?s.now-z.t:0;if(has&&age<c.ttl+c.stale)out.value=z.v;if((!has||age>=c.ttl)&&s.pending[e.key]===undefined){var t=s.next++;s.pending[e.key]=t;out.fetch.push({key:e.key,token:t})}}else if(e.type==='resolve'){if(s.pending[e.key]===e.token){s.cache[e.key]={v:e.value,t:s.now};delete s.pending[e.key]}}else if(e.type==='reject'){if(s.pending[e.key]===e.token)delete s.pending[e.key]}else if(e.type==='invalidate'){delete s.cache[e.key];delete s.pending[e.key]}out.now=s.now;out.pending=Object.keys(s.pending).sort();return{state:s,output:out}}

initial.explanation: Use single-flight caching with explicit freshness timestamps. A cached value is visible while age is below ttl+stale; refresh begins at ttl only when no request is pending. Responses affect state only when their key and token match.
initial.mapping: The cartographic rule maps cache visibility to retained map detail: stale data remains represented for a bounded window, while pending tokens preserve causality. Transfer is only an analogy; cache semantics, not geography, determine behavior.
initial.assumptions: Event fields are valid as specified, keys are lowercase ASCII, values are finite JSON, and state is supplied unchanged between events.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;var c=input.config,s={now:0,next:1,c:{},p:{}};for(var i=0;i<input.events.length;i++){var e=input.events[i],fetch=[],v=null,k=e.key;if(e.type==='advance')s.now+=e.dt;else if(e.type==='invalidate'){delete s.c[k];delete s.p[k]}else if(e.type==='resolve'){if(s.p[k]===e.token){s.c[k]={v:e.value,t:s.now};delete s.p[k]}}else if(e.type==='reject'){if(s.p[k]===e.token)delete s.p[k]}else if(e.type==='get'){var x=s.c[k],a=x?s.now-x.t:0;if(x&&a<c.ttl+c.stale)v=x.v;if((!x||a>=c.ttl)&&s.p[k]===undefined){s.p[k]=s.next;fetch=[{key:k,token:s.next++}]}}var p=Object.keys(s.p).sort(),o=output[i];if(!o||o.now!==s.now||o.value!==v||JSON.stringify(o.fetch)!==JSON.stringify(fetch)||JSON.stringify(o.pending)!==JSON.stringify(p))return false}return true;}
initial.program: function solve(x){var c=x.config,e=x.event,s=x.state||{now:0,next:1,c:{},p:{}},f=[],v=null,k=e.key;if(e.type==='advance')s.now+=e.dt;else if(e.type==='invalidate'){delete s.c[k];delete s.p[k]}else if(e.type==='resolve'){if(s.p[k]===e.token){s.c[k]={v:e.value,t:s.now};delete s.p[k]}}else if(e.type==='reject'){if(s.p[k]===e.token)delete s.p[k]}else if(e.type==='get'){var z=s.c[k],a=z?s.now-z.t:0;if(z&&a<c.ttl+c.stale)v=z.v;if((!z||a>=c.ttl)&&s.p[k]===undefined){s.p[k]=s.next;f=[{key:k,token:s.next++}]}}return{state:s,output:{value:v,fetch:f,pending:Object.keys(s.p).sort(),now:s.now}}}

final.explanation: Maintains a timestamped cache and one pending token per key. Cached values are visible through the stale interval, while refreshes begin at the TTL boundary only when no request is pending. Responses mutate state only when their token matches the current pending request; invalidation removes cache and pending state without resetting token allocation.
final.program: function solve(x){var c=x.config,e=x.event,s=x.state;if(s===null)s={now:0,next:1,c:{},p:{}};var f=[],v=null,k=e.key;if(e.type==='advance')s.now+=e.dt;else if(e.type==='invalidate'){delete s.c[k];delete s.p[k]}else if(e.type==='resolve'){if(s.p[k]===e.token){s.c[k]={v:e.value,t:s.now};delete s.p[k]}}else if(e.type==='reject'){if(s.p[k]===e.token)delete s.p[k]}else if(e.type==='get'){var z=s.c[k],a=z?s.now-z.t:0;if(z&&a<c.ttl+c.stale)v=z.v;if((!z||a>=c.ttl)&&s.p[k]===undefined){s.p[k]=s.next;f=[{key:k,token:s.next++}]}}return{state:s,output:{value:v,fetch:f,pending:Object.keys(s.p).sort(),now:s.now}}}
